messages:
jules: ran a focused priming sweep for ember8b int8 vs fp16 on multi-turn summarization. numbers look promising cost-wise but priming failures spike on citation-heavy prompts. posting short summary + suggested mitigations.
priya: paste numbers + sample failure modes pls.
jules: summary (slice=multi-turn-primed, avg convo tokens ~900, N=420):
``n- p95 latency: fp16 170ms | int8 205ms
- throughput: fp16 1.10 tok/s | int8 0.48 tok/s
- cost per 1k tokens: fp16 $0.0068 | int8 $0.0031
- conv-quality (golded F1): fp16 79.4% | int8 74.0%  (delta -5.4pp)
- citation-accuracy (manual spot): fp16 88% | int8 72%
- hallucination heuristic: fp16 1.6% | int8 6.9%
- notes: failures concentrated when system prompt includes 3+ documents and tight citation anchors
```
link: https://internal.redwood/sparkbench/ember8b/3123459999
noah: cost-per-conversation looks ~2.2x lower. for high-volume casual flows that's huge. but citation-heavy flows are risky. how big is that traffic?
jules: citation-heavy ~7% overall but ~50% of legal/enterprise workflows and most GTN demo flows. small percent but high exposure.
priya: product options: a) keep int8 default and opt enterprise/trusted flows into fp16 b) hybrid by priming complexity score c) staged A/B with human review on flagged outputs.
sam: ops levers: prefix KVCACHE for priming reduced fp16 spend historically by ~28%. alternate: decode-chunk hybrid (first N tokens in fp16 then switch to int8) to preserve priming fidelity.
noah: decode-chunk idea sounds interesting — do we have infra for dynamic precision mid-decode? might need runtime change but could be emulated by chunked requests.
jules: quick pseudocode for hybrid routing + chunking:
``n# compute priming complexity
priming_score = num_docs*avg_doc_len_normalized + citation_anchor_count*2
if priming_score >= 8:
  route -> fp16
elif priming_score >=5:
  route -> chunked: first 256 tokens fp16, rest int8
else:
  route -> int8
```
priya: for GTN decks we need: estimated monthly savings (int8 vs fp16), exposure (traffic fraction & revenue-sensitive flows), and fallback cost if we revert. can you draft?
noah: i'll model three scenarios: conservative (keep fp16 for primed flows), hybrid-chunk (chunking reduces fp16 tokens by 40%), and aggressive (int8 everywhere).
jules: rollout plan proposal:
1) 3% canary: int8 default, force fp16 for priming_score >=8 for 50% of those requests (observe both)
2) enable automated checks: citation-accuracy proxy + hallucination heuristic + user-flag metric
3) 72h live eval window -> if citation accuracy delta >4pp or hallucination rate delta >3pp -> expand fp16 to all primed flows and page #eng-ml + #product
4) after 2 weeks evaluate KV caching + chunking microbench before broader migration

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary created ember8b-int8-priming-probe @ 3% with fp16 probe for high-priming requests. See: https://internal.redwood/deploys/3123459999
gtm-bot: noted. will coordinate GTN demo owners and legal for early warnings.
priya: thanks — please post interim logs + golden eval snapshot in this thread and i'll assemble the GTN sensitivity slide.
jules: will do. posting sample failure cases separately. :mag:"
